S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and regulator review; a model may not be marketed only if the regulator determines, after review, that corrective measures are inadequate to address an unacceptable safety risk. Results must be provided in plain language to customers who buy or own that model, but individual-company per-model failure rates must not be publicly disclosed.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market release and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. Manufacturers must submit per-model results and corrective-action plans to the relevant regulator. Results must be provided in plain language to customers who buy or own that model, but individual-company per-model failure rates must not be publicly disclosed. A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and regulator review; a model may not be marketed only if the regulator determines, after review, that corrective measures are inadequate to address an unacceptable safety risk. Regulators may require retesting or additional corrective action.

judge_section_notes: The final rules set a 24-hour incident-reporting duty for all thermal incidents, which is the strongest element and benefits both firms' unreported incidents. S2 drops any numeric sales limit: the 5% failure rate only triggers review and corrective action, with sales stopping only if the regulator later finds remediation inadequate, which protects Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S5 keeps an 8-per-100k recall trigger but allows open-ended corrective action instead of recall, which protects Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9). Customer result disclosure is specified only as 'plain language' without an explicit numeric rate, so I coded it as pass/fail only; this is a judgement call.
